Alex —

Thanks for the note and for the context on timelines. We're putting together a one-page customer summary and a technical appendix. I'll attach a short executive summary and a precise timeline. High-level preview:

- Impact: increased token-latency and intermittent 5xx errors for ~8% of Greenfield production requests between 2026-02-19T22:37:00Z and 2026-02-20T01:05:00Z (PST times in the attached CSV).
- Root cause (high-level): a regression in a cache-eviction control path that caused stale KV-cache pointers to be served under specific request-shape patterns. This increased cumulative token-processing time and triggered upstream request timeouts.
- Immediate mitigations already applied: rollback of the cache-change at 2026-02-20T00:55:00Z and temporary tightening of request timeouts to avoid overload cascades.
- Next steps (estimates): full fix and additional hardening by 2026-03-03; expanded post-deploy load-test and canary policy by 2026-03-10.

I'll send the formal PDF and the supporting timeline + technical appendix in the next message. If you have a preference for wording (shorter or more technical) let me know — I can produce both an ops-facing and an exec-facing version.

Best,

Subject: Greenfield: Incident summary and action list (final)

Alex / Nadia —

Thanks for the patience while we finalized the write-up. Attached is a concise customer-facing RCA (PDF) and a technical appendix. Below is the one-page summary we recommend you share with your teams. If you'd like us to host a short 30-minute briefing for your CTO/engineering leads, we can schedule it this week.

Executive summary (one paragraph):
On 2026-02-19 at ~22:37 PST, a regression in a cache-eviction control path within Redwood's inference runtime caused stale KV-cache pointers to be referenced for a subset of requests with specific sequence-length and prompt shapes. This led to increased per-token processing time and intermittent upstream timeouts, impacting approximately 8% of Greenfield production requests for ~2.5 hours. No customer data was exfiltrated. Redwood identified the change, rolled it back, and implemented temporary mitigations; a permanent fix and additional canary hardening are scheduled.

Impact and scope:
- Affected traffic: ~8% of inference calls routed to Greenfield's model endpoint during the window.
- User-visible symptoms: token-level latency spikes (median went from ~45ms to ~220ms on affected tokens) and increased 5xx rates for a short period.
- Data exposure: none. Logs and payloads remained within normal retention; no unauthorized data access detected.

Timeline (all times in PST):
- 2026-02-19 22:37:14 — On-call alerts triggered for elevated token latency on route GF-01.
- 2026-02-19 22:44:02 — Initial investigation: correlated latency with recent runtime change in cache eviction configuration.
- 2026-02-19 23:10:48 — Deployed additional observability hooks and traced affected request shapes.
- 2026-02-20 00:55:12 — Rolled back the cache-eviction change; immediate reduction in error rate observed.
- 2026-02-20 01:05:03 — Incident declared resolved for Greenfield traffic; monitoring continued.

Root cause (concise):
A recent change to the KV-cache eviction control introduced an ordering corner case. Under a narrow combination of request sequence length and prefix cache state the runtime exposed stale cache pointers, which required extra defensive handling that significantly increased token processing time and caused upstream request timeouts.

Immediate mitigations completed:
- Rollback of the offending change (2026-02-20 00:55 PST).
- Tightened request timeouts and rate-limiting thresholds to prevent overload cascades.
- Added quick instrumentation to count stale-pointer occurrences and flag them for automatic sampling.

Planned corrective actions and owners:
- Short-term hardening: instrumentation and canary checks — owner: Markus Klein (complete by 2026-03-03).
- Permanent fix: corrected eviction logic and unit/regression tests — owner: Marissa Cole (target 2026-03-10).
- Customer follow-up: schedule a 30-min technical briefing and deliver finalized RCA PDF — owner: Soojin Lee (complete by 2026-02-23).

Attachments: redwood-rca-summary.pdf (customer-facing one-pager), redwood-technical-appendix.txt (detailed timeline + technical notes), greenfield-incident-timeline.csv (per-minute metrics slice).

Links: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1GfR-incident-briefing (detailed internal post-incident doc), JIRA INFRA-5621.

If you'd like a redacted version for public-facing release, we can prepare that as well. Please confirm if the brief is acceptable to share with your CTO; if so we'll mark the RCA as delivered and schedule the briefing.
